question: Assume today is 2026-08-17. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States in August 2026 (the number of housing units at an annual rate, as in '1,300,000'), as it will be first reported in the U.S. Census Bureau and HUD Monthly New Residential Construction release.

target.what: Seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts (new privately owned housing units started) in the United States, as first published in the Census Bureau/HUD Monthly New Residential Construction report for August 2026
target.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
target.cadence: monthly, released mid-month for the prior month (August 2026 report expected around 2026-09-17)
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-08-17 cutoff, so no August 2026 data exist; must be forecast from July 2026 level plus leading indicators. 'Privately-owned' excludes public housing (small share). 'Housing starts' counts units started, not permits; SAAR is seasonally adjusted annual rate

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 SAAR will be close to the recent trend of private housing starts (July 2026 and prior months), adjusted for month-to-month volatility; own history gives the base level and typical monthly change distribution.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly SAAR private housing starts for Jan 2024 through July 2026 (latest available before cutoff), plus August values for 2023, 2024, 2025 to gauge seasonal/level patterns; also the July 2026 first print and any June/July revisions.
search_hints: Census Bureau new residential construction July 2026 housing starts

candidates.hypothesis: Permits precede starts; the permit SAAR level and its recent trend constrain the starts level, since starts cannot persistently exceed authorized units. August starts should track permits issued in prior 1-3 months.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly SAAR building permits (total and single-family) for 2025 through July 2026, and the permit-to-start lag relationship; single-family vs multifamily split.

candidates.hypothesis: Total private starts = single-family starts + multifamily (2+ unit) starts; single-family is smoother and driven by builder sentiment/mortgage rates, multifamily is lumpy and driven by completions/absorption. Estimating each component separately reduces error.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly SAAR single-family and multifamily (2+ units) private housing starts for 2025 through July 2026; NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index for July/August 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts or nowcasts for August 2026 housing starts (e.g., from banks, Reuters consensus, Trading Economics, or prediction markets) provide a direct anchor; consensus typically within a few percent of first print.
candidates.data_to_find: Any forecast/consensus for August 2026 private housing starts SAAR published before 2026-08-17; also forecasts for July 2026 to assess forecast accuracy.

candidates.hypothesis: Mortgage rates, Fed policy, tariffs on building materials, and labor supply affect starts; a measurable shift in 30-year mortgage rate or builder sentiment between July and August 2026 would move August starts relative to July.
candidates.data_to_find: 30-year fixed mortgage rate (Freddie Mac) for July and August 2026; Fed funds path; lumber/tariff news; any weather or regional disruptions in August 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: Units under construction and completions reflect the pipeline; a large under-construction stock implies ongoing starts to sustain it, while rising completions with falling permits signal deceleration. Starts ≈ f(permits, under construction, completions).
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly housing units under construction and completions SAAR for 2025 through July 2026; relationship between under-construction stock and monthly starts.

candidates.perspective: Regional/regional permits and Census regional starts
candidates.hypothesis: Census publishes starts by region (Northeast, Midwest, South, West); the South dominates. Regional permit trends and any regional shocks (hurricanes, etc.) in summer 2026 can refine the national estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Regional housing starts and permits SAAR for 2025-2026 through July; any regional disruption news for August 2026.

June 2026 multifamily starts: Census 5+ unit figure 513,000 (p60) vs eyeonhousing 532,000 (p141) differ because eyeonhousing uses a broader multifamily definition (2+ units incl. condos); TradingEconomics 513,000 matches Census 5+ units. Definitional difference, not a contradiction.

June 2025 total starts 1,379,000, same release; useful as prior-year base for year-on-year scaling.

Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year rate series: rates rose from ~6.0% in Feb 2026 to ~6.66% by end-July and ~6.67-6.69% in early August 2026. Consistent upward drift; the August readings are the relevant ones for August starts.
15-year PMMS series, consistent with the 30-year series.
Alternative mortgage-rate measures (Lender Price, MBA) in the same 6.7-6.9% range; corroborate the PMMS level but are not independent of the same market.
MBA application volumes up modestly in early August; consistent with stable-to-slightly-improving demand, not a sharp move.
Regional June 2026 starts sum to 1,427,000 (741+248+129+309); internally consistent with the national total.
Units under construction: 1.26M total, 582k single-family, 682k multifamily, down from >1M multifamily peak in Dec 2023; consistent with a decelerating pipeline.
Completions running near or above starts, consistent with a pipeline being worked down; supports a starts level near or below recent completions.
April/March 2026 starts and permits from the same release; establish the spring 2026 level (~1.4-1.5M) before the May collapse and June rebound.
Consensus forecasts of ~1,310,000 for June 2026 (actual 1,427,000) show consensus can miss by ~9%; useful as a calibration of forecast error, not as an August anchor.
Census guidance: preliminary SA estimates revised ~1.9% on average; 6 months needed for a starts trend, 3 for permits. Sets the noise floor for any single-month forecast.
May 2026 revised +15.4% jump off a six-year low; confirms May was an unusually depressed base, so June's +19% partly reflects rebound, not trend.
Multifamily swings: -41% in May, +76.3% in June; confirms multifamily is extremely lumpy and a single month is a poor guide.
Three-month moving averages (single-family 902k, multifamily 445k) are smoother trend anchors than the June prints.
Feb 2026 actual 1.404M vs previous 1.272M; consistent with the spring 2026 level around 1.4M.
2022 TD Economics commentary: internally consistent but from a different regime (2022 boom, rates ~5%); useful only as an analogue for volatility and revision magnitudes, not for the 2026 level.

a1.role: change factor from June 2026 to August 2026 for total private starts

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed total starts (June 2026, 1,427,000) and applies a modest drift factor to August 2026. The factor is centered slightly below 1 because June was inflated by a multifamily rebound and the permit level (~1,367k) and three-month moving averages sit below the June print; the wide range reflects the ~1.9% revision noise and multifamily lumpiness. Failure mode: if July data (released just after cutoff) show a sharp move, the June anchor is stale.

p19.role: June 2026 multifamily (5+ unit) starts SAAR, the latest observed multifamily component

a3.role: change factor from June 2026 to August 2026 for multifamily starts

methods.rationale: Decomposes total starts into single-family (895k, smooth, near trend) and multifamily 5+ unit (513k, lumpy) components, each projected to August with its own factor. Single-family factor is near 1 given the 902k three-month average and 871k permits; multifamily factor is centered lower given the 445k three-month average, 496k permits, and declining under-construction stock. Failure mode: the two components share the same June release and the same macro backdrop, so errors are correlated; the multifamily factor carries most of the uncertainty.

assumptions.name: August 2026 total starts change factor vs June 2026 level
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 total starts (1,427k) were inflated by a multifamily rebound (+76.3% after -41%) and a broad regional surge; the three-month moving averages (single-family 902k, multifamily 445k) and the permit level (~1,367k) suggest the underlying trend is somewhat below the June print. Mortgage rates rose from ~6.0% in Feb to ~6.67% in August, a mild headwind. A modest downward factor with wide range reflects the ~1.9% revision noise and the lumpiness of multifamily.
assumptions.applies_when: August 2026 starts are forecast as June 2026 level times this factor, assuming no July data are available and the June-to-August drift is small and centered slightly below June.
assumptions.falsified_by: A July 2026 print far from ~1.35-1.45M, or a sharp August move in mortgage rates or builder sentiment, would overturn the centered factor.

assumptions.name: August 2026 single-family starts change factor vs June 2026
assumptions.rationale: Single-family starts fell for three consecutive months to 895k (June), with a three-month moving average of 902k and single-family permits at 871k; the segment is smooth and near trend, so a factor close to 1 with modest range is appropriate. Rising mortgage rates are a mild drag.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to project the single-family component from the June 2026 level to August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A large July single-family print or a sharp builder-sentiment drop would move the factor outside the range.

assumptions.name: August 2026 multifamily (5+ unit) starts change factor vs June 2026
assumptions.rationale: Multifamily starts are extremely lumpy (-41% May, +76.3% June); the three-month moving average is 445k vs the June 513k print, and multifamily permits (496k) and under-construction stock (682k, down from >1M peak) point to a lower sustainable pace. A downward-centered factor with very wide range reflects the lumpiness.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to project the multifamily component from the June 2026 level to August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A July multifamily print well above 513k or a surge in multifamily permits would overturn the downward center.

methods.label: m1

p3.role: June 2026 total private housing starts SAAR, the latest observed level of the target

a1.role: change factor from June 2026 to August 2026 for total private starts

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed total (June 2026, 1,427k) and applies a mean-reversion factor reflecting the multifamily spike and flat permits. Shared dependency: p3 is a first print subject to ~2-3% revision (p220). Failure mode: if July's print (unavailable) already moved sharply, the June anchor is stale.

methods.label: m2

p6.role: June 2026 single-family starts SAAR, the latest observed single-family component

a2.role: change factor from June 2026 to August 2026 for single-family starts

p19.role: June 2026 multifamily (5+ unit) starts SAAR, the latest observed multifamily component

a3.role: change factor from June 2026 to August 2026 for multifamily starts

methods.rationale: Decomposes total starts into single-family (smoother, ~63% of starts) and multifamily (lumpy) components, each anchored on its June 2026 level and adjusted separately. Single-family factor reflects the three-month decline and soft permits; multifamily factor reflects mean-reversion from the June spike. Shared dependency: both components come from the same June Census release and are subject to rev

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m2: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m1.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

m2.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

kept.name: August 2026 total starts change factor vs June 2026 level
kept.rationale: June's 1,427k was a spike driven by a 76% multifamily jump (p19/p20) after a 41% May plunge (p21); multifamily is mean-reverting and permits (p11, p13) are flat-to-down, so August should sit modestly below June. Range reflects typical monthly volatility of total starts (Census notes six months neede
kept.applies_when: June 2026 is the latest observed total and no July print is available before cutoff.
kept.falsified_by: A July 2026 print far from ~1.3-1.4M, or a large August multifamily surge.

kept.name: August 2026 single-family starts change factor vs June 2026
kept.rationale: Single-family has fallen three straight months (p23) and is -3.2% y/y (p265) with permits -2.4% m/m (p267); mortgage rates rose ~25bp from early July to early August (p100 vs p108) then eased slightly, a mild negative. Near-flat with modest downside.
kept.applies_when: Single-family trend continues its slow decline rather than reversing.
kept.falsified_by: A sharp builder-sentiment rebound or rate drop below ~6.3% in August.

kept.name: August 2026 multifamily (5+ unit) starts change factor vs June 2026
kept.rationale: June's 513k multifamily print followed a 41% May plunge and a 76% June surge (p20/p21); such swings mean-revert. Multifamily permits are 496k (p151) and under-construction stock is falling (p145), so a pullback from the June spike is likely, but the series is very lumpy so the range is wide.
kept.applies_when: Multifamily reverts toward its 3-month average (~445k, p142) rather than sustaining the June spike.
kept.falsified_by: A large multifamily permit surge or a new 5+ unit project wave in July-August.

The best estimate for the seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States for August 2026 is 1,360,458 unit/year (80% model-based interval 987,512 to 1,874,251 unit/year). This is a forecast; no August 2026 data exist as of the cutoff.

Main evidence: the June 2026 total was 1,427,000 housing units at annual rate, split into single-family 895,000 housing units at annual rate and multifamily 513,000 housing units at annual rate. Method m1 applies a total change factor of 0.97 (range 0.82 to 1.15) to the June total, giving 1,384,489 unit/year at weight 50%. Method m2 adjusts single-family by 0.99 (0.88 to 1.11) and multifamily by 0.85 (0.55 to 1.3), giving 1,336,844 unit/year at weight 50%. The two blocks are combined by geometric mean because their inputs overlap heavily, not because they are independent.

Observed: the June levels. Assumed: all change factors. Key risk: the June anchor is a first print subject to revision, and July's unavailable print may already have moved sharply. The most useful missing evidence is the July 2026 release.

Unit of the estimate: unit/year (housing units at annual rate; average over 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 August 2026 total starts change factor vs June 2026 level: 0.97 dimensionless, range 0.82 to 1.15; used by m1. Overturned by: A July 2026 print far from ~[n]-[n]M, or a large August multifamily surge.
- a2 August 2026 single-family starts change factor vs June 2026: 0.99 dimensionless, range 0.88 to 1.11; used by m2. Overturned by: A sharp builder-sentiment rebound or rate drop below ~[n] in August.
- a3 August 2026 multifamily ([n]+ unit) starts change factor vs June 2026: 0.85 dimensionless, range 0.55 to 1.3; used by m2. Overturned by: A large multifamily permit surge or a new [n]+ unit project wave in July-August.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p3 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 1,081,995 to 1,773,571; result unit unit/year converted to unit/year; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m2 formula_mc: p6 * a2 + p19 * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 1,085,226 to 1,662,585; result unit unit/year converted to unit/year; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: 2 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 1,384,489 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m2: 1,336,844 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.

The best estimate for the seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States for August 2026 is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]). This is a forecast; no August 2026 data exist as of the cutoff.

Main evidence: the June 2026 total was [[p3_value]], split into single-family [[p6_value]] and multifamily [[p19_value]]. Method m1 applies a total change factor of [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]) to the June total, giving [[m1_estimate]] [[unit]] at weight [[m1_weight]]. Method m2 adjusts single-family by [[a2_value]] ([[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]]) and multifamily by [[a3_value]] ([[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]]), giving [[m2_estimate]] [[unit]] at weight [[m2_weight]]. The two blocks are combined by geometric mean because their inputs overlap heavily, not because they are independent.

Observed: the June levels. Assumed: all change factors. Key risk: the June anchor is a first print subject to revision, and July's unavailable print may already have moved sharply. The most useful missing evidence is the July 2026 release.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
